result.decision_rationale:
The Dust effects runner can advance with an owned execution still unaccounted for. The Ghaele probes also have gaps in the late-summon control, fader readback and cleanup reporting. The retained 202648Z audio trace does satisfy the owner's conditional disposition for source-local cue tracking.

Continuation for Claude

Carry cleanup outcomes all the way to the decisions that advance the effects phase and ProbeSlot. Preserve the injected Dust failure, then account for the exact execution and every remaining resource before reporting recovery. Exercise a Ghaele result delivered after cast disposal, distinguish an absent fader from a visible one, and retain failures from early releases. Apply the same unwind discipline to the callback-withholding hook.

Use the recorded terminal playback fields in one settled cue verdict. Bind that verdict to a collector that actually ran. Preserve both original effects failures, the accepted R4-F5 disposition and the unknown cause of 164749Z. Update the active handoff with the accepted Ghaele scope and completed validation expenditure.

Keep the corrections within the existing fixtures, gameplay choices and owner amendments. Both authorized product builds are spent. The reported 39m04s leaves 20m56s of the combined validation allowance. Use immutable observations and separately deployable harness corrections where they cover the finding. If a necessary RuntimeTesting correction requires another product candidate to establish native behavior, record that precise blocker after safe restoration. The existing authority provides no third build.

findings.actual: Both 200320Z and 202648Z record the named removal failure and ownedExecutionsLive=1 at abandonment. After waiting, S7DustAbandoned checks the repaired buff and tint count but never reads that execution again. It sets isolationRestored=true, later samples run, and the final phase check reads only the ordinary Dust cell.
findings.blocking_rationale: The runner reports successful isolation without establishing what happened to the execution it observed still running.
findings.expected: The injected failure reaches the enclosing verdict. Recovery permits continuation only after the exact execution and every independent release are accounted for.
findings.requested_correction: Keep an exact execution or ledger readback through the recovery wait. Include residual executions, commands, conditions, subscriptions, hooks and repair failures in the abandonment result consumed by the continuation guard and final phase check.
findings.requested_evidence: Show the named injected failure first, followed by the exact execution's settled state before advancement. A still-live or unreadable execution, or another failed release, must stop later cells and fail phase restoration.
findings.title: Carry the abandoned Dust execution through the final isolation decision
findings.trigger: The early cast applies Sickened, its removal fails during disposal, and the owned execution remains live after its command leaves the queue.

findings.actual: The positive case now verifies the exact pending command and grant and keeps a separate witness subscribed for six seconds. The negative control waits until spawnHandle.Summoned is populated, then disposes spawnRun. Its late-owned-summon verdict uses a count acquired before disposal. A witness that lost correlation at disposal would still pass this control.
findings.blocking_rationale: The requested negative case has not exercised the interval that the independent witness exists to cover.
findings.expected: A controlled owned result first delivered after cast-owner disposal is detected during the late-spawn window and fails the pending verdict.
findings.requested_correction: Drive the negative control through disposal before delivering the correlated result. Keep the witness read-only. Have its caller account for any positively identified late unit or fail isolation before advancing.
findings.requested_evidence: Show the ordered disposal and delivery, zero owned results before disposal, the exact late result afterward, the failed verdict, the intact foreign control and the witness unsubscribe.
findings.title: Deliver the negative-control summon after the cast owner is disposed
findings.trigger: A pending cast produces its owned summon after its handle has been removed from the cast owner's list.

findings.actual: GhaeleLighting.Valid now rejects a literal false or missing field. Its producer calls EntityFadedIn, which returns true when GetComponent<EntityFader>() returns null. A live view with no fader therefore serializes the same faderVisible=true value as a visible fader. Removing the field in the domain test misses this producer path.
findings.blocking_rationale: An unavailable subject readback can still qualify as positive visibility evidence.
findings.expected: Visible, hidden and unavailable subject-fader observations remain distinguishable from capture through verdict.
findings.requested_correction: Distinguish component presence and Visible at the Ghaele observation boundary. Preserve the shared capture helper's established behavior for other callers. Qualify retained rows to the extent their component presence can be established.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise a missing component through the producer and reader, alongside present-hidden and present-visible controls. Use existing identity or presence evidence for the retained rows where available. Preserve the owner-accepted interior scope.
findings.title: Distinguish an absent Ghaele fader from a visible fader
findings.trigger: The captured Ghaele has an enabled body renderer and a live view whose EntityFader component is unavailable.

findings.actual: OwnedDisposables.Destroy marks the unit requested before calling destroy. Direct calls such as units.Destroy(first) in Lifecycle can throw outside ProbeCleanup. Poll records a test error, final releases skip the marked unit, and CleanupReport can remain successful. The witness-move release similarly records a still-held, unfinished move only in witnessSettled. ProbeSlot bases isolation solely on CleanupReport.
findings.blocking_rationale: The Ghaele lifecycle step permits continuation after a test failure when isolation is reported restored. An early release failure can therefore leave owned state in the next step.
findings.expected: Every failed early release reaches the cumulative cleanup report while each unit still receives at most one destruction request.
findings.requested_correction: Record failures from direct destruction and an unsuccessful witness settlement in the same cleanup outcome consumed by ProbeSlot. Preserve per-item attempts and the original test error.
findings.requested_evidence: Through ProbeSlot, make a direct destruction call throw before final release and exercise a witness that remains held after settlement. Require a named cleanup failure, one destruction request, continued independent releases, failed isolation and refusal to start the next probe.
findings.title: Return failed early Ghaele releases to ProbeSlot
findings.trigger: An immediate unit destruction throws, or the exact witness move remains active after its release action returns.

findings.actual: S7CallbackLoss writes the hook count and disposal failures in its finally block. Its verdict runs after that block, so iterator disposal skips the verdict. On ordinary completion, a failed Sprint25Check also leaves the caller free to enter Dust. The effects phase's final restoration predicate never reads the callback-hook outcome.
findings.blocking_rationale: A failed unpatch can leave a hook on the product callback receiver while the phase reports restored isolation.
findings.expected: Once the observer acquires its callback hook, its release result governs phase restoration and admission to later cells on every exit.
findings.requested_correction: Give the enclosing effects runner the callback-hook cleanup outcome during unwind. Stop advancement on residual hooks or unpatch failure and include that outcome in the final restoration decision.
findings.requested_evidence: Dispose the enclosing runner with the callback hook acquired and an unpatch failure injected. Show the named failure at phase level, continued independent cleanup and refusal to advance. Retain the observed zero-hook control.
findings.title: Propagate callback-hook cleanup through effects-phase abandonment
findings.trigger: The callback-loss observer is abandoned while yielded, or its Harmony unpatch fails.

findings.actual: CallbackLossVerdict accepts any inactive sample in the window. Neither survivorAtWindowEnd.playback nor survivorAfterDisposal.playback is an input. Changing the latter in the retained 202648Z row from inactive to playing leaves the offline verdict unchanged.
findings.blocking_rationale: The evaluator can declare that only bookkeeping remained even when its own terminal observation reports active playback. The actual 202648Z terminal observations were inactive.
findings.expected: A characterization accounts for the exact ID's playback at the window end and after source disposal, including contradictory or unavailable terminal evidence.
findings.requested_correction: Judge the recorded terminal playback states in the settled verdict. Keep query results, actual callbacks and stop requests distinct.
findings.requested_evidence: Alter only the terminal observations of a copy of the retained row. Playing or unresolved terminal playback must prevent characterization. Re-evaluate the original immutable rows with the same reader.
findings.title: Make terminal playback observations part of the callback-loss verdict
findings.trigger: A survivor is sampled inactive earlier and a required terminal read subsequently reports playing or unknown.

findings.actual: After the last package at 740d94a995, c9c4c33154 moved live reads of the stop records to the end of the window and added otherRetirementSettled. The head's Focused test instead reads the retired ID from cuesAtEnd and derives the survivor's stop status from the retained row. It verifies a historical interpretation. Neither native package executed the new sampling path.
findings.blocking_rationale: The validation policy and OWNER AMENDMENT 2 require affected native evidence for a changed observer. The retained evidence supports the product disposition but does not exercise the final collector.
findings.expected: The delivered collector has an affected native observation, or the correction is confined to a reader over fields the exercised collector already produced.
findings.requested_correction: Bind the settled evaluation to the exercised collector and its immutable fields, or use a genuinely separate authorized harness over an existing package. Keep the collector identity and the offline verdict explicit.
findings.requested_evidence: Show the source-to-collector identity and the applicable reader result. If required live sampling still differs and cannot be exercised under the two-build cap, retain the specific validation blocker.
findings.title: Bind the settled cue evaluation to the collector that actually ran
findings.trigger: Use the final candidate's in-game callback-loss observer as the qualified observation path.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The active packet description and sections 4.5 and 4.7 agree with the manifest. Of twelve isolated clips, two sample current cues and ten are alternatives. Trumpet 397 posted on frame 4975 and its 37.09 m reading was taken on 4976.

The probe applies AutoPass to the correlated save and leaves the dice native. In 201133Z the direct foreign die inside the owned save rolled 8 against control 8, the owned die rolled 17 against control 17, and the following draw matched. The abandonment record shows the subscription released.

The shared ledger now carries the named removal failure into the inner verdict. In both effects runs that verdict also records one live execution. The outer recovery decision never rechecks it and allows the sampling cells to run.

Teardown releases the exact attacks and disposable target without a unit-wide LeaveCombat call. In 201333Z the independent control and Ghaele remained in combat across teardown, no owned attack remained, and native combat exit followed the control's release by 3.04 seconds.

OWNER AMENDMENT 2 section 4 withdrew the requirement to clear a missing-callback record before its own source is disposed when playback ends normally and isolation is demonstrated. In 202648Z both IDs were live. Only 684 received the first stop. The product callback for 656 was withheld at 2.20 seconds, its native ID read inactive through the rest of the window, and its tracked component and view were observed destroyed on its own retirement. The hook count returned to zero. This establishes the conditional limitation for that run. The cause of the historical 497 failure remains unknown.

The pending preconditions, separate subscription and positive six-second observation are present in 201333Z. The controlled spawn was already observed before its owner's disposal. The requested post-disposal detection case remains unverified.

The reader now checks cutout, unknown signatures and readable disagreement before withholding positive credit for a null body. The focused gate exercised the five-positive-plus-contradiction cases. Both retained round-5 datasets still have eleven positive rows and zero contradictions.

Literal false and missing serialized fields now fail the reader. The actual producer converts a missing EntityFader into a true field, so an unavailable subject observation can still pass the complete capture path.

The probe registers the exact witness before submission and releases it in the same poll after the survival readback. In 201333Z it was held and unfinished on both sides of combat teardown, then settled. R6-F1 covers reporting a failed settlement.

Final unit releases are enumerated after iterator disposal, and a request is recorded before destruction. The executed ProbeSlot regression with deferred destruction requests the shared target once. R6-F1 concerns a direct request that throws outside the cleanup report.

The 180635Z extract contains 33 passing structured checks. The concurrent-retirement predicates pass in 154136Z and 161344Z, fail in 164749Z, then pass in 170720Z and 180635Z. The corrected chronology and count agree with the active record.
